holidays.name: National Fast Food Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the drive-thru, the dollar menu, and the glorious convenience of getting a hot meal in under five minutes without ever leaving your car.
holidays.origin: An unofficial American food observance that grew out of the fast food boom of the 20th century and is promoted mostly by restaurant chains and social media.
holidays.funFact: The first drive-through window is often credited to Red's Giant Hamburg in Springfield, Missouri, which opened in 1947 and served soldiers who were not allowed to leave their cars in uniform.

holidays.name: National Button Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the humble button, the little disc that keeps your pants up and your coat closed. Collectors, sewers, and fashion fans honor the fastener in all its shapes and sizes.
holidays.origin: Observed unofficially by button collectors and craft groups, with ties to the National Button Society, which was founded in 1938 and promotes button collecting as a hobby.
holidays.funFact: Buttons were originally used as decorations rather than fasteners, and buttonholes did not appear in Europe until the 13th century.

holidays.name: International Day for Tolerance
holidays.description: A serious but important observance encouraging respect, understanding, and appreciation of the rich diversity of cultures and ways of being human. Expect workshops, school events, and a lot of thoughtful conversation.
holidays.origin: Proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly in 1996 after UNESCO adopted a Declaration of Principles on Tolerance on November 16, 1995.
holidays.funFact: The UNESCO-Madanjeet Singh Prize for the Promotion of Tolerance and Non-Violence is awarded in connection with this day.

holidays.name: Oklahoma Statehood Day
holidays.description: Oklahomans celebrate becoming the 46th state with pride, parades, and probably a bit of barbecue. It is a day to honor the Sooner State's history, culture, and wide open prairies.
holidays.origin: Oklahoma was admitted to the Union on November 16, 1907, when Indian Territory and Oklahoma Territory were combined into a single state.
holidays.funFact: Oklahoma's nickname, the Sooner State, comes from settlers who sneaked into the Unassigned Lands to claim territory sooner than the legal start time of the 1889 land run.

holidays.name: National Role Play Gamers Day
holidays.description: Roll the dice and grab your character sheet. This day honors tabletop adventurers, dungeon masters, and anyone who has spent six hours arguing with friends about whether a goblin can be persuaded.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance created by and for the gaming community to celebrate role-playing games like Dungeons & Dragons, which first launched in 1974.
holidays.funFact: The first edition of Dungeons & Dragons was initially printed in a run of just 1,000 copies, and it sold out in about 11 months.
